analysis.headline: SUSE Week 46: volume is kernel, risk is Pillow, Docker, ProFTPD and Node.js
summary: 1928 CVEs across a full distribution, of which 1405 are the Linux kernel and 229 are MozillaFirefox; only 488 touch anything outside the base OS. The severity split (55 critical, 1841 important, 31 moderate, 1 low) comes from the vendor and barely discriminates, so triage score and EPSS carry the analysis. There are no KB articles here: this is a SUSE advisory and package stream, and treating it as a Microsoft-style KB release misreads the remediation path — patching is by package and image rebuild, not by monthly rollup.

Risk does not follow volume. Both KEV entries sit outside the kernel — Node.js (CVE-2026-111497) and Docker (CVE-2026-31431) — and the highest-EPSS item is a pre-auth ProFTPD flaw at 0.95. Pillow contributes eight criticals in a narrow EPSS band, which is a supply-chain signal rather than eight independent incidents. Meanwhile our own enrichment reports zero exploited, zero disclosed, zero remote-unauthenticated and zero more-likely, which contradicts the newsroom's own pre-auth RCE coverage and should be read as unpopulated fields, not safety.

themes.title: Pillow's clustered criticals are a build-pipeline problem
themes.detail: Eight critical image-parsing flaws in python-Pillow, CVSS 8.1–9.8, EPSS 0.42–0.71, most flagged automatable. None is a listening service; the exposure is CI, thumbnailers, upload handlers and content ingestion that link or shell out to Pillow.

themes.title: Both KEVs are outside the kernel
themes.detail: CVE-2026-111497 is the Node.js Brotli/HTTP2 issue our desk has covered ten times under two names; CVE-2026-31431 is the Docker flaw now used by IoT botnets with public Linux exploit chains. A Docker cluster of four further CVEs sits alongside it, so container hosts need one coordinated update pass.

themes.title: Internet-facing daemons: ProFTPD and Apache beat their severity labels
themes.detail: ProFTPD CVE-2026-42167 carries EPSS 0.95, the highest in the release, and was not tagged automatable — a scoring gap worth trusting the number over the flag. Apache's 9.8 CVE-2026-119618 has EPSS 0.76 and no newsroom coverage, while the published Apache story covers CVE-2026-106023, which does not appear in the risk top 30.

themes.title: Kernel bulk is local privilege and memory corruption, not remote
themes.detail: Seventy-three percent of the release by count, with automatable flags on CVEs scoring 7.0–8.2 and EPSS in the 0.4–0.6 band. Individually modest; collectively they justify a scheduled reboot wave rather than emergency handling, except where container escape or hypervisor boundaries are in scope.

themes.title: EOL crypto and base libraries are the quiet tail
themes.detail: openssl-1_0_0 and openssl-1_1 still ship in this stream, with CVE-2026-84782 automatable at EPSS 0.61; glibc gets four fixes and openssl-1_1 five. These are inherited by every image built on the distro, so they outlive the advisory window.

analysis.data_vs_prose: The machine record claims zero exploited, zero disclosed and zero remote-unauthenticated against a release the newsroom has already described as pre-auth RCE in ProFTPD and Apache and as a KEV-listed Node.js flaw — those counters are not populated, and quoting them as findings would be wrong. The EPSS buckets are internally contradictory (4 at ≥10% versus 59 at ≥50%), so use per-CVE EPSS values, not the aggregate. Conversely the prose misses the shape: eight Pillow criticals with only three partially covered, a five-CVE Docker cluster, and the fact that neither KEV is a kernel issue. Two Pillow headlines (CVE-2026-112393, CVE-2026-112403) are copy-pasted from the CVE-2026-112900 headline, and the covered Go and Node items point at CVE-2026-97033 and CVE-2026-105482/105483/106069 while the top-scored Go item is CVE-2026-97040 — coverage follows stories, not scores.

watchlist.why: EPSS 0.95 pre-auth ProFTPD, large exposed population, untagged as automatable — highest real-world likelihood in the release
KEV Node.js flaw, most-covered by press, so exploitation attempts are already circulating under multiple names
KEV Docker issue with public Linux exploit chains in IoT botnets; container hosts are the blast radius
Apache 9.8 at EPSS 0.76 with no newsroom coverage — highest-severity unpublicised network-facing item
Worst of the Pillow cluster at 9.8, EPSS 0.71, automatable; representative of the whole eight-CVE set
Automatable OpenSSL fix on a branch that should not still be deployed
Docker at EPSS 0.94, automatable, second-highest likelihood after ProFTPD

analysis.patch_note: Order: nodejs24 and docker/containerd first (both KEVs, both reachable from build and runtime paths), then proftpd and apache2 on any host with a listening socket, then python-Pillow wherever images are parsed or generated — including CI images, not just servers. Rebuild base images for openssl-1_0_0, openssl-1_1 and glibc before the next kernel reboot window rather than after it. Linux kernel and MozillaFirefox make up the bulk by count (1405 and 229) and can go in the scheduled maintenance pass; only prioritize kernel where container escape or guest-to-host boundaries matter. Expect no KB-style rollup: track per-package advisory IDs and verify image digests, since with_kb is zero across the release.
